A stopwatch was started when 50 cm3 of a 0.20 M sodium thiosulfate solution was poured into a conical flask containing 10 cm3 of 1.0 M HCl solution. The conical flask was put standing on top of a black cross marked on white paper. The time for the cross to become obscured by the precipitate produced in the reaction was measured. The reciprocal of this reaction time (1/t) was taken as a measure of the initial rate of the chemical reaction. The stock 0.20 M solution of sodium thiosulfate was then diluted with deionised water to produce 50 cm3 each of 0.16 M, 0.12 M, 0.08 M, 0.04 M and 0.02 M solutions in turn.
